clue.text: Quiz a body of conservationists with some mistrust

parts.note: to quiz someone is to ask them questions
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage and countryside charity

explanation.surface: Someone questions a conservation charity while harbouring doubts about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Askant is an old form of askance, looking sideways with suspicion or doubt.

clue.text: A man long incarcerated in appalling little place

indicators.note: the convict and the abbreviation sit inside the word for appalling

parts.note: appalling means vile
an old lag is a convict long kept in prison

explanation.surface: A long-serving prisoner is held in a dreadful little settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'old lag' is British slang for a convict who has served a long sentence, so 'incarcerated' supplies the lag; 'in' then places it, with L for long, inside the word for appalling.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet or small rural settlement is a modest place, smaller than a town.

clue.text: Endorsement certain to encompass giant merger

indicators.note: the word for certain wraps around the rearranged letters

parts.note: certain means sure

indicators.note: a merger mixes things together, so the letters of giant are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A guaranteed approval for a huge corporate merger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merger' scrambles the five letters of giant; 'to encompass' tells you the word for certain wraps around that jumble. 'Endorsement' is the definition, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing a document is the act that endorses it, so a name written in ink is an endorsement.

clue.text: Holding catch to be returned to the river

indicators.note: returning something sends it back, so the word for catch is read backwards

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England, common in crosswords

explanation.surface: A fish caught is thrown back into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be returned' turns NET into TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is the holding of land, property or an office, as a tenant does.

clue.text: The new bosses' haunt

indicators.note: making something new remakes it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe adds no letter

explanation.surface: Ghostly talk about the new managers' favourite hangout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haunt' looks like a noun (a favourite spot), but it is the verb: to preoccupy constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: To obsess someone is to prey on their mind constantly, just as a fear or memory haunts them.

clue.text: Inequitable? Indeed so — quite wrongly

indicators.note: doing something wrongly gets it out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a ruling is unfair and the reply agrees it was badly done.
explanation.definitionFit: A biased, partial judgment favours one party, so it is unfair or inequitable.

clue.text: This country's made the health-resort popular

parts.note: a spa is a resort with mineral springs for health treatments
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A nation boasts that its spa town has become a fashionable destination.
explanation.definitionFit: A European nation on the Iberian peninsula, here referred to as this country.

clue.text: Like a star taking a letter in say

indicators.note: the letter's name is placed inside the word for say

parts.note: to say is to state
ell is the spelt-out name of the letter L

explanation.surface: A celebrity takes a letter while speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellate is a botanical and zoological term for star-shaped, radiating from a centre.

clue.text: Vivacious when well-supplied with alcohol?

explanation.surface: A lively person who has been drinking plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively people are full of spirit; and spirits are strong drink, so something laced with them is jokingly so described.

clue.text: Tells of disquieted religious leaders

indicators.note: read as dis-quieted, it means with the quiet sign, P for piano, taken away

parts.note: prelates are bishops and other senior clergy

explanation.surface: Someone reports on clergy who are troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disquieted' seems to mean anxious, but split as 'dis-quieted' it removes P (piano, quiet in music).
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or recount it.

clue.text: Nobody's to be left out, even though exhausted

explanation.surface: Everyone is included even though they are worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-in deal includes everyone or everything; informally, all in also means completely worn out.

clue.text: "Quota", a French article showing good sense

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allotted share or quota
le is the French masculine definite article, the

explanation.surface: A French newspaper article on quotas proves sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoned basis behind something, the logic that makes sense of it.

clue.text: A member of a jolly group

parts.note: Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, so the group is the RM, Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Someone belongs to a cheerful band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective for cheerful, but it is a nickname for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb of the body is called a member, and the upper limb is one such.

clue.text: Got there possibly simultaneously

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Two people perhaps arrived at the same moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening at the same time means things occur in unison or at once.

clue.text: A game of cards in the car tends to absorb children

indicators.note: the answer sits within the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: Kids play cards in the back of the car on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Écarté is a two-player card game popular in nineteenth-century France.

clue.text: Force cheat to make a real effort

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat them
to strain is to exert oneself hard

explanation.surface: Someone forces a cheat to try really hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to compel or oblige them.

clue.text: Strange individual

explanation.surface: An odd person.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar means odd or weird; it also means belonging distinctively to one person or thing, particular.

clue.text: The villain's epitaph

explanation.surface: The words carved on a scoundrel's gravestone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rip is an old word for a rascal or rogue; and the gravestone inscription stands for requiescat in pace, rest in peace.

clue.text: Enters without permission and is turned out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A trespasser is caught and thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge in where one is not invited or wanted is to trespass.

clue.text: Notice love causes turmoil

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
love is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A personal advertisement about romance creates a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss, bustle or commotion, as in 'much ado about nothing'.

clue.text: Sailors received about a thousand

indicators.note: the word for received goes round the other letters

parts.note: seen can mean received, as visitors are seen or received
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Sailors were welcomed in their thousands.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariners or men of the sea crew a ship.

clue.text: A civil engineer-a highly-skilled person

explanation.surface: A civil engineer is described as an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is an expert, someone outstandingly good at something.

clue.text: A growth industry

parts.note: a booming business sector in the surface, but literally the industry of growing crops and livestock

explanation.definitionFit: Agriculture is literally the business of making things grow: cultivating crops and raising animals.

clue.text: Even opposing a good man, a social worker

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
ST, saint, is the crossword abbreviation for a good man
an ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: Someone is even opposed to a decent person who works for social services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a welfare officer; it is an ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant means steady and unchanging, like an even pace or temperature.

clue.text: Held in trust for a clever and very wise man

indicators.note: held in means the letters are contained within the run of these words

explanation.surface: Money held in trust for a bright, sage person.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a person of great wisdom whose advice is treated as infallible.

clue.text: Kind offer

explanation.surface: A generous bid.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender means gentle and caring; it is also a formal bid or offer, as in putting work out to tender.

clue.text: Drink with stout defender

parts.note: to sup is to drink
porter is a dark beer, close kin to stout

explanation.surface: A loyal fan who takes a drink of stout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like an adjective for brave or sturdy; it is a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer or champion defends a cause or a person.

clue.text: Leapt about — a bit of a bloomer

indicators.note: about signals the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone jumped around after a small mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder; it is a flower, of which this is a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower blooms, and one of its coloured leaves forms part of the bloom.

clue.text: Gold turned over to a fellow citizen

indicators.note: turning something over reverses it, so the word for gold is read backwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a man is a fellow, a chap

explanation.surface: Gold handed over to a fellow resident.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of ancient or modern Rome is so called.

clue.text: It may be inapt to serve guinea-fowl

indicators.note: may be signals one possible rearrangement of these letters

parts.note: to do is to serve, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: Serving guinea-fowl might be inappropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Pintado is a name, from Portuguese for painted, for the speckled guinea-fowl.

clue.text: The union will get everyone a nice settlement

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: a settlement arranges matters, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trade union will win everyone a pleasant deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or association of parties for mutual benefit.

clue.text: Exercises for bores

explanation.surface: Training routines for tiresome people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bores' seems to mean dull people; it is tools that bore holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Drills are military or training exercises; they are also tools that bore holes.
